free_tier.stated: No storage quota of its own — it serves the npm registry, so the ceiling is npm's ~100 MB publish limit. Probed 28.3 MB, 32.2 MB, 54.0 MB and 64.5 MB single files: all HTTP 200, all full length, sha256 identity with hop.js on the 54 MB and 64.5 MB cases. No per-file cap was encountered.

egress.terms: Free, no account, Cloudflare-fronted (cf-cache-status HIT on repeat). No published bandwidth limit.

tooling: GET https://unpkg.com/<pkg>@<ver>/<path>. Also /<pkg>@<ver>/ (directory listing) and ?meta. Plain curl/rclone.
chaining: Second mirror in a 3-way npm serving tier (unpkg + hop.js + jsDelivr). Because all three read the same npm tarballs, publishing once to npm gives you three independent free CDNs with different per-file ceilings — jsDelivr 50 MB, unpkg and hop.js effectively npm-bounded. Shard at 45 MB and every mirror serves every shard.
limits_note: per-object-cap: npm publish-side (~100 MB tarball, 413 above that). No cap observed on the read side up to 64.5 MB. Version pinning required for immutability.
reliability_note: Long-running but small-team; Cloudflare absorbs the bandwidth. Was 403 on the .exe? No — unpkg served it; it is jsDelivr that blocks the extension.

evidence.proved: HTTP 200, 87,533 bytes, sha256 fc9a93dd… matches jsDelivr and githack copies (probed)
